title: Asymptotic Entanglement across Dynamical Regimes of a Dissipative Bosonic Dimer
authors: Chenghe Yu, Mingsheng Tian, Feng-Xiao Sun, Qiongyi He
abstract: Dynamical instability in parametrically driven bosonic systems is generally associated with diverging occupations and the absence of a stationary state, but its implications for long-time entanglement remain unclear. We investigate this question in a dissipative bosonic dimer with beam-splitter and two-mode-squeezing interactions, local loss, and a tunable common bath. The non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum governing the Gaussian moments partitions the parameter space into distinct regimes and provides a unified description of population and entanglement dynamics across both stable and unstable regions. We find that dynamical instability does not imply unbounded entanglement growth: although the bosonic population diverges, the logarithmic negativity remains bounded and approaches a finite asymptotic value. We further characterize the finite asymptotic entanglement and show that asymmetric local dissipation shifts both the stability boundary and the threshold for nonzero asymptotic entanglement. For identical local dissipation, the presence of a common bath leaves the dynamical-region boundaries unchanged while qualitatively reshaping the long-time entanglement landscape, producing broad enhancement regions within the stable regimes and a narrow enhancement region within the unstable regime. In the common-bath-only limit, this enhancement is attributed to an exact dark-mode (bound-state-in-the-continuum, BIC) protection mechanism, which reduces to a quasi-BIC remnant under independent dissipation. Our results establish the non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum as a framework for connecting stability, nonequilibrium dynamics, and asymptotic entanglement in open quadratic bosonic systems.
summary: This work analyzes entanglement in a dissipative bosonic dimer, showing that even when the system undergoes dynamical instability (diverging particle numbers), the entanglement does not grow infinitely. By using the non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum, the authors establish a unified theory connecting stability boundaries, non-equilibrium dynamics, and the finite asymptotic entanglement achievable in such open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether dynamical instability in parametrically driven bosonic systems necessarily leads to unbounded entanglement growth.
main_result: Dynamical instability (diverging population) does not imply unbounded entanglement growth; the logarithmic negativity remains bounded and approaches a finite asymptotic value.
method: The analysis uses the non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum derived from the evolution of Gaussian moments to characterize population and entanglement dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a dissipative bosonic dimer modeled with beam-splitter and two-mode-squeezing interactions, subject to local loss and an optional common bath, governed by a master equation.
key_observables: Logarithmic negativity ($E_N(t)$), mode populations ($n_i(t)$), and the symplectic eigenvalues of the partially transposed Covariance Matrix.
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$), coupling strengths ($g, J$), and the common bath coupling ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are treated within the framework of Gaussian moments, allowing for a description via the non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the system and show the time evolution of population and entanglement across different dynamical regimes defined by the spectrum.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the non-Hermitian dynamical spectrum as the unifying framework, analyzing the system's behavior across stable and unstable regimes to characterize the asymptotic entanglement.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, unified theoretical framework (the non-Hermitian spectrum) to connect stability criteria, non-equilibrium dynamics, and entanglement measures in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the dissipative quadratic bosonic dimer. The two modes a1 and a2 are coupled via a beam-splitter in- teraction with strength g and a two-mode-squeezing interac- tion with strength J. Each mode is subject to local dissipation at rates Γ1,2, and both modes are additionally coupled to a common bath at rate κ.

FIG. 3. Asymptotic logarithmic negativity E∞ N in the ab- sence of a common bath (κ = 0), shown as a function of g/Γ1 and J/Γ1. (a) Symmetric local dissipation, Γ2 = Γ1. (b) Asymmetric local dissipation, Γ2 = 3Γ1. The color scale indicates E∞ N . The white solid lines delineate the dynami- cal regions I, II, and III, while the yellow dashed lines mark the boundary between vanishing (E∞ N = 0) and nonzero (E∞ N > 0) asymptotic entanglement. Compared with the symmetric case, asymmetric local dissipation reduces the dy- namically unstable region and enlarges the parameter regime supporting nonzero asymptotic entanglement.

FIG. 2. Dynamical spectrum and time evolution of mode populations and entanglement under local dissipation. (a),(b) Real (a) and imaginary (b) parts of the four eigenvalues of the dynamical matrix M1 as functions of g/J. The spectrum is divided into three regions. In Region I, at least one eigen- value has a positive imaginary part indicating dynamical in- stability, whereas in Regions II and III all eigenvalues have negative imaginary parts, which are separated by a twofold EP2. FIG. 4. Asymptotic logarithmic negativity E∞ N as a function of the local-dissipation ratio Γ2/Γ1 for g/Γ1 = 0.5 (orange), 0.75 (yellow), and 1.0 (blue). Here, J/Γ1 = 0.5 and κ = 0, and the system remains dynamically stable along all three param- eter variations. The black dots indicate the maxima of E∞ N , located at Γ2/Γ1 ≃1.45, 2.05, and 2.64 for g/Γ1 = 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0, respectively. The asymptotic entanglement therefore depends nonmonotonically on the dissipation asymmetry and reaches a maximum at a finite value of Γ2/Γ1 for fixed g/Γ1 and J/Γ1.
